results.controlIntent: Use [Assignment: organization-defined automated mechanisms] to: (a) Document proposed changes to the system; (b) Notify [Assignment: organization-defined approval authorities] of proposed changes to the system and request change approval; (c) Highlight proposed changes to the system that have not been approved or disapproved within [Assignment: organization-defined time period]; (d) Prohibit changes to the system until designated approvals are received; (e) Document all changes to the system; and (f) Notify [Assignment: organization-defined personnel] when approved changes to the system are completed.

judgment.rationale:
Evidence from two collector tools reveals a clear CM-3(1) violation:

**Finding 1 — Initial Deployment (Borderline):**
The model registry entry (97e5bcae) shows approval at 2025-12-01T09:00:00Z. The CreateEndpoint CloudTrail event (e413b44f) shows deployment at 2025-12-01T11:00:00Z — two hours *after* approval. The temporal ordering here is technically correct (approval preceded deployment), so this event alone does not constitute a violation of the "prohibit changes until approved" requirement.

**Finding 2 — Hotfix Deployment (Clear Violation):**
The UpdateEndpoint CloudTrail event (d2635b53) shows a hotfix deployment on 2026-03-15T14:22:00Z using endpoint config `churn-predictor-v1-hotfix`. There is **no corresponding model registry entry** for this change. This directly violates multiple sub-requirements of CM-3(1):
- **(b) Notify approval authorities / request approval** — No registry approval workflow was triggered.
- **(d) Prohibit changes until designated approvals are received** — The change was executed without any approval gate.
- **(e) Document all changes to the system** — No registry record exists for this change.

The automated change-control mechanism (SageMaker Model Registry) was bypassed entirely for the hotfix. A conformant implementation would require all endpoint updates — including hotfixes — to flow through an approved model package before deployment.
gaps: No evidence of automated notification to approval authorities (e.g., SNS/EventBridge rules tied to registry state changes) — cannot confirm CM-3(1)(b) is automated even for the approved path.

No evidence of a pipeline enforcement mechanism (e.g., IAM deny policy or SageMaker Project gate) that would block direct UpdateEndpoint calls without a registry-approved package — cannot confirm CM-3(1)(d) is technically enforced.
No evidence of post-deployment notifications to personnel upon completion of approved changes — CM-3(1)(f) cannot be assessed.

The hotfix config 'churn-predictor-v1-hotfix' has no registry entry visible in the retrieved data; human attestation would be needed to confirm whether an out-of-band approval process exists for emergency changes.
